description: Hi! We're Team Break_Point, exploring the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge. We're students still learning — not experts — but excited to dive into NASA's fire data and figure things out as we go, using AI tools to help us build.
summary: The NASA Fire Calendar is an advanced web application designed to track, monitor, and analyze wildfire data. It helps users visualize historical climate patterns, hot spots, and active fire events using interactive calendar-based data visualization and a map interface. The project integrates a robust backend and a responsive frontend architecture to make complex environmental data easily accessible, actionable, and transparent for disaster monitoring and early warnings.
details:
• What it does / How it works: The project is a web-based calendar and tracking application designed to monitor wildfire data. It utilizes a decoupled architecture with a React frontend user interface and a FastAPI backend server that handle data processing, API integration, and rendering fire event logs or calendar views.

Benefits & Intended Impact: It provides an accessible tool for tracking historical and active fire data, helping users and researchers better visualize environmental risks, hot spots, and climate patterns through an organized calendar interface.

Tools, Coding Languages, & Software Used:

  • Frontend: React (deployed on Vercel)
  • Backend: Python FastAPI, PostgreSQL / psycopg2
  • Version Control: GitHub repositories (nasa-fire-calendar-frontend and nasa-fire-calendar-backend)

Creativity: The project emphasizes a clean separation of concerns between client-side map visualization and server-side data routing, complete with a custom sensor harmonization feature for enhanced data accuracy.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
